facts.statement: Jeholosaurus is a small neornithischian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China.
facts.quote: Jeholosaurus is a genus of small neornithischian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous-aged Yixian Formation of what is now China.

facts.statement: The first specimens were discovered in 2000 at Lujiatun near Beipiao City, Liaoning Province, China, and described by Xu Xing, Wang Xiaolin, and You Hailu.
facts.quote: The first two Jeholosaurus specimens were found in 2000 at Lujiatun near Beipiao City, Liaoning Province, China, and named and described the same year by Xu Xing, Wang Xioalin and You Hailu.

facts.statement: The genus name Jeholosaurus means "lizard from Jehol," referring to a historical province in western Liaoning and northern Hebei.
facts.quote: The generic name Jeholosaurus means "lizard from Jehol"; Jehol is the name of a historical province situated in western Liaoning and northern Hebei.

facts.statement: The type specimen for the genus is cataloged as IVPP V 12529.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Jeholosaurus, on which the genus is based, is IVPP V 12529.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 126 to 124 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was found in a layer of the early Yixian Formation, dating from the Barremian, about 126-124 million years old.

facts.statement: The fossils were preserved in fluvial sandstone and tuff, likely buried by a volcanic eruption that affected a radius of fifty to sixty miles.
facts.quote: The layers consist of fluvial sandstone interspersed with tuff and it is thought that an enormous volcanic eruption occurred burying everything within a fifty to sixty-mile radius.

facts.statement: Four additional specimens, including partial and complete skulls, were referred to the species in 2009.
facts.quote: In 2009, 4 new well-preserved specimens were referred to Jeholosaurus: IVPP V15716, a partial skull; IVPP V15717, a complete skull; IVPP V15718, a complete skull; IVPP V15719, a partial skeleton.

facts.statement: Jeholosaurus was a small, bipedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Jeholosaurus was a small bipedal herbivore.

facts.statement: The holotype measures 71.1 cm in length with a tail measuring 35.6 cm.
facts.quote: The holotype is 71.1 cm long with a 35.6 cm long tail, nearly half the length of the complete animal.

facts.statement: The skull of the holotype is 6.3 cm long, and each lower jaw is 5.9 cm long.
facts.quote: The length of the skull is 6.3 cm and the lower jaws of the mandible are 5.9 cm each.

facts.statement: The premaxilla contains six teeth, while the maxilla has at least thirteen teeth.
facts.quote: The premaxilla has six teeth and the maxilla has at least thirteen teeth.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Jeholosaurus may have been omnivorous because its front teeth resemble carnivores while its back teeth are fan-shaped like herbivores.
facts.quote: Although the back, maxillary, teeth are fan-shaped like those of a plant eater, the front premaxillary teeth are narrower and longer, more like a carnivorous dinosaur. This may mean that Jeholosaurus was omnivorous, eating both plants and animals.

facts.statement: Jeholosaurus replaced its maxillary teeth every 46 days, a rate faster than most basal ornithischians.
facts.quote: Jeholosaurus had a very rapid rate of maxillary tooth replacement at 46 days, more rapid than most basal ornithischians.

facts.statement: The foot has four metatarsals, with metatarsal III being the longest at 5.5 cm and positioned more anteriorly.
facts.quote: The foot has four metatarsals. The longest is metatarsal III, with a length of 5.5 cm; it is placed more anteriorly than the other metatarsals.

facts.statement: The original describers classified Jeholosaurus only as Ornithischia incertae sedis without assigning it to a specific family.
facts.quote: The describers did not assign Jeholosaurus to any family, limiting themselves to a placement as Ornithischia incertae sedis.

facts.statement: Later cladistic analyses placed Jeholosaurus in a basal position within the Ornithopoda.
facts.quote: Later cladistic analyses have recovered a basal position in the Ornithopoda.

facts.statement: A clade containing Jeholosaurus, Haya, and Changchunsaurus was named Jeholosauridae.
facts.quote: They named this clade Jeholosauridae.

facts.statement: Jeholosaurus lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 124 million years ago, between the late Barremian and early Aptian, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 124 millones de años, entre el Barremiense superior y el Aptiense inferior, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The species is classified within the family Jeholosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Jeholosauridae

facts.statement: Jeholosaurus shangyuanensis is the only known species in the extinct genus Jeholosaurus.
facts.quote: Jeholosaurus shangyuanensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Jeholosaurus

facts.statement: Jeholosaurus was a small bipedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Jeholosaurus era un pequeño herbívoro bípedo.

facts.statement: The premaxilla has six teeth and the maxilla has at least thirteen teeth.
facts.quote: El premaxilar tiene seis dientes y el maxilar tiene al menos trece dientes.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Jeholosaurus may have been omnivorous, eating both plants and animals, due to its mixed dentition.
facts.quote: Esto puede significar que Jeholosaurus era omnívoro, comiendo tanto plantas como animales.

facts.statement: The deep ventral margin of the maxilla suggests that fleshy cheeks may have been present.
facts.quote: El margen ventral profundamente insertado en el maxilar sugiere que las mejillas carnosas pueden haber estado presentes.

facts.statement: The foot has four metatarsals.
facts.quote: El pie tiene cuatro metatarsianos.

facts.statement: The third metatarsal is 5.5 centimeters long and is positioned more anteriorly than the others.
facts.quote: El metatarsiano III con una longitud de 5,5 centímetros. Se coloca más anterior que los otros metatarsianos.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in the lower Yixian Formation dating to the early Aptian, approximately 126 million years ago.
facts.quote: Se encontró en una capa inferior de la formación Yixian, que data del Aptiano temprano, de unos 126 millones de años.

facts.statement: The sedimentary layers consist of interbedded fluvial sandstone and tuff, believed to be deposited by a massive volcanic eruption covering an 80 to 96-kilometer radius.
facts.quote: Las capas consisten en arenisca fluvial intercalada con toba y se cree que se produjo una enorme erupción volcánica que enterraba todo dentro de un radio de 80 a 96 kilómetros.

facts.statement: The original describers did not assign Jeholosaurus to a family, classifying it only as Ornithischia incertae sedis.
facts.quote: Los descriptores no asignaron Jeholosaurus a ninguna familia, limitándose a una ubicación como Ornithischia incertae sedis.

facts.statement: The time range for Jeholosaurus is from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the family of Jeholosaurus as Thescelosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Thescelosauridae

facts.statement: Both known skulls are incomplete and required partial restoration.
facts.quote: Ambos cráneos están incompletos y tuvieron que ser parcialmente restaurados.

facts.statement: A distinctive feature is that the claw of the third toe is longer than the other phalanges of that same toe.
facts.quote: La garra del tercer dedo del pie es más larga que las otras falanges del tercer dedo del pie.
